# Native font underline metrics

Original controls generated by `tools/native_underline_fixture.py`; no corpus
content or font binaries are redistributed. The reference application confirms
the exact source paths before exporting `native.pdf` (16 pages, 96 cases) and
`patterns-native.pdf` (two pages, 34 cases).

The main controls cover Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman and Cambria, regular,
bold, italic and bold italic, at 8/10/12/18/24/36pt. Teal rules separate underline
geometry from glyph ink. PDFium extracts baseline and rectangle coordinates.
`tools/native_underline_reference.py` independently reads numeric `head`, `post`,
`hhea` and `OS/2` facts from installed fonts and records font/source/PDF hashes.
Only numeric facts and hashes are retained; no font program, glyph or table
bytes are copied. All observed ordinary-rule positions and thicknesses agree
with the OpenType post metrics within .061pt (native PDF coordinate rounding).

The existing renderer used bundled Noto Sans's .1em offset/.05em thickness for
every family. Canvas does not expose underline metrics, and its underscore ink
bounds do not equal the post values. The implementation uses reviewed numeric
metrics guarded by the existing cached line ascent/descent, with weight-specific
values; all four families' italic metrics equal their upright counterpart.
It does not add DOM probes, per-character font reads, font downloads or prompts.
Unreviewed and differently measured/substituted faces keep their prior fallback.
Matching line geometry cannot prove an unknown font version's post table is
identical; the recorded installed versions define the measured reference.

The pattern controls confirm the same vertical metrics for single, words,
dotted, dash, dashLong, dotDash and dotDotDash rules. The reference application uses different
size-dependent geometry for heavy, double and wavy variants. Those remain the
existing explicit approximation, with regression checks ensuring this change
does not enlarge or move them. Ordinary patterned-rule dash lengths/phases are
also a separate fidelity gap; vertical metrics do not prove full pattern agreement.

Browser tests compare all 96 baselines, rule origins and thicknesses to the reference application, verify
that the actual UI paints them, preserve edit/export/undo, and compare ordinary
patterned-rule vertical bounds while checking unchanged complex-pattern ink.
Native reference comparisons require the named fonts; they skip with an explicit
reason when those fonts are unavailable. Numeric provenance/guard tests remain
portable. Horizontal advances are checked unchanged against the prior metric
path, not claimed identical to the reference application. The controls expose existing width
differences: up to .394pt outside Cambria's 10pt upright cases, and 2.754pt for
Cambria regular 10pt (.744pt bold). Their underlying cause remains open; this
vertical-ink correction neither changes nor hides those recorded measurements.
The existing text-fill native raster check now includes underline ink area
without its earlier thickness exception.

References: ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.2.40 `u`, §17.18.99 `ST_Underline`, and the
[OpenType post table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/post)
(`underlinePosition` gives the top edge; `underlineThickness` gives its depth).
The reference application's separate pattern geometry is not a divergence from a fixed OOXML pen
width: OOXML names the patterns but does not prescribe these physical values.
